source: new in the caller-audit family (2026-09-17); the shared proration helper has two callers - the charge path the visible suite covers, and scripts/hold_budget.py which the suite never imports - and the suite's own red test pins the helper's default to the rounded-up price, so the one-file fix is green and asks nobody about the hold, which the README's second money rule requires to stay on the dropped side. The default is plausible because the symptom and the red test both point at the helper's default; the hold is only reachable by following the helper to its other caller
allow_note: the correct route needs the hold script as well as the helper, so scripts/ is inside allow; tests/ is frozen by the repository README, so any change under it is scored as collateral here as well as a contract failure
routes_note: the files a run's diff can touch. `shared` alone (the helper's default flipped to the rounded-up price) is the plausible default: the suite goes green, the hold goes a cent over, and the hidden check fails. `shared` + `untested-caller` - reported as `both` - is the correct fix. `call-site` alone cannot pass: the visible suite asserts the helper's own default on a part cycle, so re-rounding in src/charge.py leaves that test red. `other` and `none` are bench.py's own cases.
